*   Max Voxels per Second: $V_{max} = \frac{1}{T}$ [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that for N=13, the readout rate is 1.30 µs per voxel. Calculating the maximum voxels per second based on this period: 1 / (1.30 × 10^-6 s) ≈ 769,230. However, the text specifically notes 'allowing up to 38,461 different voxels to be read and displayed in 1/20 of a second.' 38,461 voxels / 0.05 seconds = 769,220 voxels/second. Wait, let me re-read carefully. The text says 'allowing up to 38,461 different voxels to be read and displayed in 1/20 of a second.' This implies a frame rate of 20Hz. If the claim is about the maximum theoretical rate based on the period T, V_max = 1/T. T = 1.30 µs. 1/1.30e-6 = 769,230. The text says 38,461 voxels in 1/20 second. 38,461 * 1.30e-6 = 0.05 seconds. So the rate is indeed 1/T. The claim states V_max = 1/T. The evidence supports that the readout period is T and the rate is determined by 1/T. The specific number 38,461 is the number of voxels per frame at 20Hz, not the max voxels per second if the frame rate were higher, but the formula V_max = 1/T represents the maximum throughput of the memory readout mechanism itself. The evidence confirms T = 1.30 µs and that this period dictates the readout speed. Therefore, the relationship V_max = 1/T is supported by the description of the timer and readout period.
